title: Endpoint / EndpointSlice v1beta watches are dropped — CoreDNS 1.11 needs Kubernetes 1.21+

detection.reason: the question is whether the API server LACKS discovery.k8s.io/v1; detection kinds assert presence (API_VERSION_IN_USE on that group would fire on every current cluster), EndpointSlices are not collected, and the served API versions are not in the snapshot

quote: we have dropped support for watching Endpoint and Endpointslice v1beta, since all supported K8s versions now use Endpointslice.
remediation: Upgrade Kubernetes to 1.21+ (discovery.k8s.io/v1) BEFORE CoreDNS to 1.11; on an older API server the kubernetes plugin has nothing to watch and service resolution stops.
verifyCommand: kubectl api-versions | grep -cx discovery.k8s.io/v1  # 0 = this API server cannot serve EndpointSlice v1, so CoreDNS 1.11+ has nothing to watch — upgrade Kubernetes to 1.21+ BEFORE CoreDNS
coversNotes: plugin/kubernetes: remove Endpoint and EndpointSlice v1beta Support

title: bufsize: the default advertised size rises to 1232 (was 512)

detection.reason: the size is a directive-line argument, which is not collected; only the directive's presence is

quote: The _bufsize_ plugin changed its default size limit value to 1232
remediation: A bare `bufsize` directive now advertises 1232 bytes instead of 512: fewer truncations and TCP retries, but responses between 513 and 1232 bytes can now be IP-fragmented on paths with a small MTU (the upstream README's own caveat). Pin `bufsize 512` to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*bufsize\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed bufsize line with no size argument changes to 1232 at 1.11.0

title: forward plugin metrics changed

detection.reason: Prometheus rules and dashboards are not collected

remediation: Re-validate alerts and dashboards built on `coredns_forward_*` series against a 1.11 instance; 1.11.0 changed them and 1.11.0's own follow-up restored some for compatibility.
verifyCommand: kubectl get prometheusrules -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec | tostring | test("coredns_forward_")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # rules printed use forward-plugin series that changed at 1.11.0
coversNotes: plugin/forward: fix forward metrics for backwards compatibility

title: health: the health endpoint self-polls localhost by default

detection.reason: runtime behaviour of the health endpoint

remediation: A `health` block bound to a non-loopback address is probed via localhost from 1.11.0; adjust `health <addr>` if the probe target must differ.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*health\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed health directive self-polls localhost after 1.11.0

title: The container image runs as a non-root user

detection.reason: pod securityContext and volume permissions are not in the collected projection

remediation: The 1.11 image runs as a nonroot uid. Manifests that force `runAsUser: 0`, mount the Corefile/certificates root-only, or bind a hostPort under 1024 without NET_BIND_SERVICE need adjusting; port 53 in-container still works via the binary's file capability.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("coredns"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name): runAsUser=\(.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsUser // .spec.template.spec.containers[0].securityContext.runAsUser // "unset") runAsNonRoot=\(.spec.template.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot // .spec.template.spec.containers[0].securityContext.runAsNonRoot // "unset") hostPorts=\([.spec.template.spec.containers[].ports[]? | select(.hostPort != null) | .hostPort | tostring] | join(","))"'  # runAsUser=0 pins the old root behaviour and a hostPort below 1024 needs NET_BIND_SERVICE once the image runs as nonroot

title: dns64: SERVFAIL when no next plugin is configured

detection.reason: plugin order in the Corefile is fixed by CoreDNS, and whether a resolver follows dns64 is a Corefile fact the projection reduces to directive names

quote: Return RcodeServerFailure when DNS64 has no next plugin
remediation: A server block with `dns64` but no upstream (forward) after it now answers SERVFAIL instead of an empty answer; add the upstream the synthesis needs.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*dns64\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed dns64 block needs a forward after it

title: tls: certificate paths are resolved against the root plugin's directory

detection.reason: certificate paths are directive-line arguments, which are not collected

quote: plugin/tls: respect the path specified by root plugin
remediation: In a server block that also sets `root`, relative `tls` file paths are now resolved under that directory (they were resolved from the working directory). Use absolute paths or move the files.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(tls|root)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a block printing both root and a relative tls path resolves the certificates differently after 1.11.2

title: kubernetes: PTR records only for endpoints that define a hostname (1.11.4; reverted in 1.12.1)

detection.reason: which pods define a hostname and which clients do reverse lookups are not knowable from the projection

quote: plugin/kubernetes: only create PTR records for endpoints with hostname defined
remediation: At 1.11.4 reverse lookups for pod IPs behind headless Services answer only when the endpoint sets a hostname; 1.12.1 reverts this. If reverse resolution matters, skip 1.11.4 and go to 1.12.1+.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*kubernetes\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # the printed kubernetes block stops answering hostname-less PTRs at exactly 1.11.4

title: file: a zone file that fails to parse is an error, not a partial load
quote: plugin/file: return error when parsing the file fails
remediation: A zone file with a syntax error used to load partially; from 1.11.4 file.Parse reports the error — at startup this stops CoreDNS, at reload the old zone stays. The auto plugin loads its directory through the same parser (plugin/auto/walk.go), so its zone files are affected too. Validate every zone file before the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(file|auto)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed file zone / auto directory must parse cleanly on 1.11.4+
